title: First VLT color photo of a strange galaxy
caption: The ring galaxy NGC 4650A, imaged by the Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This color photo from ESO's Very Large Telescope shows NGC 4650A, a complex system with two clearly separate parts. One is a lens-shaped galaxy of type S0. The other is a knotty, extended ring of stars, dust and gas that wraps around it, and the two are set nearly at right angles to each other.

A lens-shaped, or lenticular, galaxy has a disc and a central bulge but little ongoing star formation. Seeing one encircled by a ring tilted almost perpendicular to it is unusual, and the high resolution makes both parts easy to tell apart.

NGC 4650A belongs to the Centaurus chain of galaxies, lying in the southern constellation that shares its name, about 165 million light-years away according to the caption. The composite combines several blue, green-yellow and red exposures taken with the VLT Test Camera, carefully processed to sharpen the final result.

understand.summary: This composite was made with the VLT Test Camera from B (blue), V (green-yellow) and R (red) exposures. The source does not publish the exact color mapping beyond these band names.
understand.eye: The system is far too faint to see this way by eye, and the exposures and processing bring out detail no eye could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The field measures 1.5 by 1.5 arcminutes, and the final image sharpness reached about 0.53 arcseconds.
alt: A lens-shaped galaxy encircled by a knotty ring of stars, dust and gas set nearly at right angles to it.
